publisher: National Center for Health Statistics, CDC
title: Short Interpregnancy Intervals in 2014: Differences by Maternal Demographic Characteristics
authors: Marie E. Thoma, Casey E. Copen and Sharon E. Kirmeyer
universe: Second and higher-order singleton births in 2014 to residents of the 47 states and the District of Columbia that used the 2003 revision of the birth certificate (about 96% of U.S. births)
limits: The interpregnancy interval runs from the previous live birth to the conception of this one. The median is published only as a band of months, not a point. National only: no state figures. Read through the fetch tool; a plain download from the cloud returns Access Denied.

medianInterval.quote: The median interpregnancy interval was 24–29 months, or 2–2.5 years.

shortIntervals.label: Under 18 months
shortIntervals.quote: Overall, 28.9% of U.S. mothers who had a second or higher-order birth in 2014 had a short interval of less than 18 months.

shortIntervals.label: 12 to 17 months
shortIntervals.quote: Interpregnancy intervals of 12–17 months (13.4%) were the most common of all short interval categories.

use: renewalTimingPeakYears: the timing pull peaks at the middle of the median band, 24 up to 30 months, so 27 months or 2.25 years; the band's own 2 to 2.5 years is the spread. The share under 18 months is the band the year run checks the town's births against (scripts/research/people-year.ts).
